subject: Post-incident: log snapshot review — no customer records accessed
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@synergybank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident: log snapshot review — no customer records accessed

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our conversation, I've attached the log snapshot and a short hash summary from the timeline we discussed (2026-09-04 01:00 UTC — 2026-09-04 04:30 UTC). Monica ran the log reconciliation and a targeted index search for Synergy Bank identifiers.

Quick summary up front:
- No outbound network flows containing customer PII or whole-record payloads were identified in the impacted runtime windows.
- We observed retries and elevated error rates on a small subset of inference requests; those requests did not include customer payloads matching your account identifiers.
- Chain-of-custody and access logs (read access to object store) show only internal operator activity tied to the mitigation.

Attachments: log-snapshot-20260905.tar.gz (log-archive), hash-summary-20260905.csv, redwood-incident-brief.pdf

Next steps: Monica will share the verification checklist and the query strings used so you can reproduce the checks; if you want, we can coordinate a short recording session to walk through the queries.

Camila Reyes
Security Response Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@synergybank.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Synergy Bank Security Team <sec-team@synergybank.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident: log snapshot review — no customer records accessed

Camila,

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we close this:
1) For the query strings Monica used — can you confirm if they included both hashed and unhashed customer identifiers? We need to reconcile against our hashed-at-rest keys.
2) You mention "no outbound flows containing customer PII" — can you confirm whether payload-level inspection included both request and response bodies?

If the above checks are reproducible, Synergy will be satisfied with a final statement confirming no customer records were exposed and the hash manifest to match against our records.

Thanks,
Laura Gomez
Head of Information Security
Synergy Bank

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@synergybank.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident: log snapshot review — no customer records accessed

Hi Laura — hi Camila,

Answering your questions:
1) Query coverage: we ran searches against both unhashed identifiers (where present) and the hashed identifier fields we store in the request index. For your raw logs we also computed the same SHA-256 hashes you use internally and matched them against the hashed index. The query strings are attached as a text snippet in the Drive link (see related links).
2) Payload inspection: we examined request bodies (incoming payloads) and response bodies from the inference runtime. Responses are logged with metadata only unless explicitly configured to persist content; in this window we have content for a tiny subset of internal diagnostic requests — none of which map to Synergy Bank account identifiers.

I ran a deterministic hash comparison and exported a small manifest (hash-summary-20260905.csv) — each hash in that file maps to either (a) known internal service IDs or (b) redacted test fixtures. No customer hashes matched.

If helpful I can share a short walkthrough video tomorrow showing the queries and the hash reconciliation steps.

—Monica
Senior Forensics Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@synergybank.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident: log snapshot review — no customer records accessed

Monica — thank you, that helps. Please proceed with the walkthrough video and include the exact hash algorithm string you used (e.g., SHA-256, UTF-8 normalization). Also please attach the manifest to this thread when ready. We will run the manifest check against our key store and reply with a short confirmation.

Best,
Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@synergybank.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final confirmation: no customer records accessed — incident closure note

Hi Laura,

Following Monica's verification and the reconciliation exercise we completed with Synergy's team, this is an official closure note from Redwood:

- We have completed a deterministic, end-to-end review of request/response logs and object-store access for the implicated timeline (2026-09-04 01:00 UTC — 2026-09-04 04:30 UTC).
- The hash manifest (hash-summary-20260905.csv) sent to you contains SHA-256 hashes computed over the same canonicalization steps discussed on the call (UTF-8 normalization, trimmed whitespace).
- No hashes in the manifest matched Synergy Bank customer identifiers.
- There is no evidence of data exfiltration, and no unauthorized read operations on customer data stores were observed.

Attachments included in this message: redwood-incident-brief.pdf, hash-summary-20260905.csv

If you would like a signed attestation on company letterhead we can provide that via DocuSign; otherwise consider this email a formal customer impact closure statement for the incident.

Thanks again for working closely with us through the verification steps.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
